_readme: Story arcs for survivors. Edit freely; /survivors arcs reload applies it live (or restart). personas: keyed by persona number 0-9 (see Personas.java). Each persona has 4 beats in order: memory, request, skill, closing. A beat unlocks at its trust (45/60/75/90 by default) AND its trigger: talk (small talk while the survivor is idle at home), watch (after a night on guard), protected (a player stood by them when scared, or they were just rescued), quest:day:N (world day), quest:dims:N (N other dimensions visited). Lines are cut at 130 chars. {name} = the survivor's name. request beats: place.where = rail | building | basement | city (where in the ruins the chest goes); item/item_name = the keepsake to hand back; reward = items in the chest (id*count). skill: steps are crew actions (gather, stock_up, make, build, dig, farm, light_up, store, pick_up...). closing effect: lantern | surname | avoid (namespace of a horror mod).

hints: ...anyone... fourth floor... they're on the stairs...
...can anyone hear this... the door won't hold... please...
...east stairwell... three of them... I can hear them breathing...
...is this thing on... I'm alone in here... they know I'm in here...
...station office... barricaded... it's quiet now, and that's worse...
freed: I thought the stairs were the end. Get me out of here.
Don't let go of the light. I'll follow you.
arrive_crew: Walls. A door. I'll earn my place, I swear.
Lights on, all of them. I'll never complain about a lantern again.
arrive_guest: Not much room, but a roof. I'll stay out of the way.
I'll sleep by the door. If there's a spare corner, I'll take it.
gone: The signal went quiet. Whoever it was, they're gone.

lines: Day forty-one. The whistle blew and the platform filled. I checked every ticket. Every one.
Forty trains left that night, on time. I stamped the last. Then the tunnel behind it went dark.
The Engine turns at the end of the line. I know because the trains stopped coming back.
beats.gist: You told them about the night of the evacuation: forty trains left on time, then the tunnel went dark.

lines: There's a ticket punch in my station office, line four. My father's. I won't leave it down there.
It's marked on your map. Mind the stairs.
beats.gist: You asked them to fetch your father's ticket punch from a station office; they did.
thanks: My father's punch. Click, click, like the old days. You ride free, anywhere on the line.
Passage anywhere. I'll write it on a ticket.
reminder: Line four, the station office. The punch has my father's initials.
No hurry. The office has waited this long.

lines: Nobody runs late with a timetable. I wrote the crew one.
Wood, torches, lights on. In that order, every day.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a daily timetable routine.

skill.name: {name}'s timetable
skill.description: gather wood, stock torches, light the camp

lines: I'll keep a lamp lit by the gate. A signal for anyone still out there.
Every line needs a light at the end.
beats.gist: You keep a lantern lit by the gate every night, as a signal for anyone still out there.

lines: Ha. Haha. Sorry. I kept the pumps running under the station. Forty-one days, never a leak.
Then every gauge dropped at once. The lamps went out one tunnel at a time. Ha.
I climbed out through the vents. I didn't look back. I never look back.
beats.gist: You told them you ran the station pumps until every gauge dropped and the tunnel lamps went out.

lines: I left my wrench roll in the pump room. Basement, under a station. I can't go back alone. Ha.
It's marked. Please. Bring it up.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring your wrench roll up from a pump room under a station; they did.
thanks: My wrench roll! Every size, still oiled. Ha! Free repairs for life.
I'm not crying. That's gear oil.
reminder: The pump room, under the station. Third door, the one that hums.
Take your time. Ha. No. Not too much time.

lines: Fine. Machines run on routine. Here's mine, for the crew.
Tools first, then chests. Nothing rusts on my watch.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a tune-up routine: tools first, then the chests.

skill.name: {name}'s tune-up
skill.description: make spare stone tools and store them

lines: I heard it down there. Breathing in the pipes.
I'm not going near the Cave Dweller again. Don't ask me to. Ha.
beats.gist: You will never go near the Cave Dweller again; you heard it breathing in the pipes.

lines: What's in it for me? Fine. I picked the Fall clean. Warehouses, flats, the lot.
Found a train once, doors open, seats still warm. Nobody aboard. I took the shoes and ran.
Funny thing about the evacuation. They left their bags. Every single one.
beats.gist: You told them you scavenged the empty city, and that evacuees left every bag behind.

lines: I stashed my good satchel under a stairwell in the old district. Fetch it and we're even.
Marked. Don't open it first. I count everything.
beats.gist: You asked them to retrieve your good satchel from under a stairwell; they did.
thanks: Huh. You brought it. All of it. Fine. We're even. Mostly.
...Thanks. Don't tell anyone I said that.
reminder: Under a stairwell, old district. Look for the scratched door.
Still waiting. Not that I care.

lines: You want my trick? Pick up everything that isn't nailed down.
Then check the pockets. Twice.
beats.gist: You taught the crew your sweep routine: pick everything up, then store it.

skill.name: {name}'s sweep
skill.description: pick up loose items and store them

lines: That tall thing in the treeline. I watched it follow us all night.
I'm done with Kenny. I won't go near him again, whatever you offer.
beats.gist: You will never go near Kenny again after he followed the group all night.

lines: I baked all night when they evacuated. Two hundred loaves. Nobody was hungry, but they took them anyway.
A little girl held one on the platform like a teddy bear. The train pulled out. She was still holding it.
So I keep baking. Somebody out there might want a loaf.
beats.gist: You told them about baking two hundred loaves the night of the evacuation, and the little girl who held one.

lines: My mother's sourdough starter is in a crock in a bakery by the old market. I left it on the shelf.
It's still alive, I can feel it. Marked on your map.
beats.gist: You asked them to fetch your mother's sourdough starter from a bakery in the ruins; they did.
thanks: It's bubbling! Oh, you wonderful people. Fresh bread tomorrow, I promise.
Every loaf carries a bit of the old city now.
reminder: The bakery by the old market. The crock has a blue lid.
It's a stubborn starter. It'll wait.

lines: You kept me safe, so here's my best secret: bake in bulk.
Grow it, gather it, stock it. Nobody goes hungry.
beats.gist: You taught the crew your batch routine: gather crops and stock bread.

lines: We never kept last names, we just said 'the baker.' Put down Bellweather.
My mother's name. The bread deserves it.
beats.gist: You took the last name Bellweather, your mother's name.

lines: I preached on the platform that night. 'The dark has teeth,' I said. They called me mad. Then it bit.
I carried the chapel lamp down the tunnel. It burned three days. I swear it did.
The scripture is made up, friend. The dark is not. That part I did not make up.
beats.gist: You told them you warned the platform that the dark had teeth, and carried the chapel lamp through the tunnel.

lines: The chapel lamp still hangs where I left it, in the vestry. Bring it home and the dark will hesitate.
Marked on your map. May light go before you.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring the chapel lamp home from a vestry in the ruins; they did.
thanks: The lamp! It still burns! Do you see? Light is the only scripture.
Bless your boots, friend.
reminder: The vestry, behind the altar. Follow the smell of lamp oil.
The lamp waits. It is more patient than I am.

lines: Keep vigil with me a night and I'll show you the oldest rite: light every dark corner.
Torches, torches, torches. That is the whole sermon.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a vigil routine: light the camp and stock torches.

skill.name: {name}'s vigil
skill.description: light dark spots and stock torches

lines: I will keep a lantern lit at the gate every night, until the dark learns manners.
Do not put it out. That is the one commandment.
beats.gist: You keep a lantern lit by the gate every night.

lines: Everyone says 'before the Fall' like it was a place. I only know what the walls remember.
My dad left me a radio. It only plays static. But at night the static counts backwards.
Day forty-one. That's what it says. Over and over. Does that mean anything to you?
beats.gist: You told them about your father's radio, which counts down to 'day forty-one' in the static.

lines: I hid my best gadget in a ventilation duct. Brass thing, tick-tock. A flat in the city, second floor.
It's marked. Watch for loose floors. I mean it.
beats.gist: You asked them to fetch your brass gadget from a ventilation duct in the city; they did.
thanks: It still ticks! Okay, that's a little emotional. Don't look at me.
Here, take this. I mean the spare gear. It's lucky. Probably.
reminder: Second floor, a flat with a green door. The duct's behind the stove.
It's fine, it's a very patient gadget.

lines: Okay, so I built a trick for furnaces and chests. Wanna see?
It's not magic. It's doing things in the right order.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a gadget run: build a furnace and a couple of chests.

skill.name: {name}'s gadget run
skill.description: make a furnace and two chests

lines: People keep asking my last name. I never had one. I want Kettle.
It's loud, it whistles, it keeps warm things warm. That's me.
beats.gist: You took the last name Kettle, because it whistles and keeps warm things warm.

lines: Squad of eight. Nine with the dog. We held the east gate until the horn.
Last order was 'fall back to the platform.' I fell back. They didn't.
I keep count. Forty-one so far. Squad would say go for fifty.
beats.gist: You told them your squad of eight held the east gate and you were the only one who fell back to the platform.

lines: My squad badge is on the guardhouse desk at the east gate. Third floor, gray door.
Marked. No fuss. Just bring it.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring back your squad badge from the east gate guardhouse; they did.
thanks: That's it. Third squad, east gate. Thank you. That's... thank you.
I'll watch your back from now on. Not a promise. An order.
reminder: East gate guardhouse. Third floor. Gray door.
Still there, I'd bet. Nobody steals a badge.

lines: Perimeter's a habit. Fence, lights, eyes open.
Do it every night and nothing walks in.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a perimeter routine: a tall fence and lights.

skill.name: {name}'s perimeter
skill.description: fence a ring around the spot and light it

lines: Angels. I saw one move when my squad blinked.
I'm never going near one again. Court-martial me.
beats.gist: You will never go near a Weeping Angel again; you saw one move when your squad blinked.

lines: I can't say what I worked on. Only that it hummed. Low. Under the capital.
We called it the Engine. Clean power, we said. The night it switched on, the dark started to come up.
Day forty-one, I signed the evacuation order myself. I don't tell people that.
beats.gist: You told them the Engine hummed under the capital and that you signed the evacuation order.

lines: My notebook is in the lab sublevel, under a desk with a cracked leg. The Engine's specs.
Marked. Bring it to me before someone reads it. Don't read it.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring back your lab notebook with the Engine's specs; they did and did not read it.
thanks: Ah. It's all here. The numbers don't lie, they only judge.
You didn't read it. I can tell. Thank you.
reminder: The lab sublevel. The desk with the cracked leg.
Please. I'd rather it were in my hands than anyone else's.

lines: Core samples. Dig small, learn big.
Careful where you sink it. Some things sink back.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a core-sample routine: dig a narrow hole and store the finds.

skill.name: {name}'s core samples
skill.description: dig a narrow shaft and store what comes up

lines: I've seen the Nexus. It's the Engine's shadow, grown up wrong.
I'm not going near it again. I made enough mistakes.
beats.gist: You will never go near the Infection Nexus again; you think it is the Engine's shadow.

lines: I played the platform that last night. Nobody applauded. They kept getting on the trains.
The lute cracked when the crowd pushed. I kept playing four strings. The dark didn't care.
Somewhere in the tunnels a whistle blew in B-flat. I've been trying to find that note since.
beats.gist: You told them you played the platform on the last night and that a whistle in B-flat still haunts you.

lines: My lute case is in the cloakroom at the old station. Line four, left lockers. The letter inside, I never sent.
It's marked. Not the lute. The letter.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring back an unsent letter from a locker at the old station; they did.
thanks: Ah. Her handwriting, my handwriting. I'll read it to the stars.
Thank you. This verse is yours.
reminder: Line four, left lockers. The case has a green strap.
It's waited this long. So have I.

lines: Work goes faster with a tune. I wrote one for the crew.
Wood, then stone, one verse each.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a work song: wood, then stone.

lines: I always signed Larkin on my posters. Nobody remembers them. I do.
Let the name be spelled right this time.
beats.gist: You took the last name Larkin, the one you signed on your posters.

lines: My fields went under the concrete in one season. The city just grew over them.
Wheat came up through the cracks that first spring. I cried. Then I harvested.
Forty-one days of food on those trains. I grew some of it.
beats.gist: You told them your fields were paved over by the city, and that wheat still came up through the cracks.

lines: My old plowshare is in a shed under the overpass, where the market was. Rusty. Good.
It's marked on your map.
beats.gist: You asked them to bring back your plowshare from a shed under an overpass; they did.
thanks: The old share, still sharp! Good iron doesn't forget.
First furrow's yours.
reminder: The shed under the overpass. By the old market.
Rain's coming, I can smell it. But it'll keep.

lines: Plant what you eat. Eat what you plant. Walk the rows twice.
That's the whole trick.
beats.gist: You taught the crew a planting routine: tend the fields.

skill.name: {name}'s planting
skill.description: tend the farm for a while

lines: A farmer keeps a light on for whoever's late home.
I'll keep a lantern at the gate. If you're out in the dark, look for it.
beats.gist: You keep a lantern lit by the gate every night for anyone late home.
